test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Two straight lines CD and AB cut each other at point O. Angle AOD = 80^circ . What is the value (in degrees) of angle AOC ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary (Linear Pair).

Sum of angles = 180°

∠AOC = 180° − ∠AOD

∠AOC = 180° − 80° = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Straight lines AB and CD intersect at point O.

Angle AOD = 80°.

**Formula Used:**

Linear Pair Axiom: If a ray stands on a line, then the sum of two adjacent angles so formed is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2aa679e0e37c81678824aa0738af2870dfcc10aa48822f9a48c4979a3b2b71bf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since CD is a straight line and ray OA stands on it:

⇒ ∠AOD + ∠AOC = 180°

⇒ 80° + ∠AOC = 180°

⇒ ∠AOC = 180° − 80°

⇒ ∠AOC = 100°

**∴ The correct answer is 100°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite to each other are equal. Here, ∠AOD = ∠BOC = 80° and ∠AOC = ∠BOD = 100°.

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are called supplementary if their sum is exactly 180°.

Sum of Angles at a Point

The sum of all angles around a single point where lines intersect is always 360°.
